blocks.title: Translate requirements into responsibilities
paragraphs: The purpose of class design is to make a complete program understandable and testable. Start from required behavior and data relationships; a noun in a story does not automatically need its own class.

blocks.title: Separate domain values from access to them
paragraphs: An original roof-inspection tool records RoofSection(id, area), Inspection(sectionId, status) and a list of inspections. A RoofSection is a domain value. A ReportService answers questions such as which sections lack a completed inspection. A parser turns external text into those values.

Use composition when an object has another object or collection. Introduce inheritance or an interface only when a real substitution contract needs different implementations. Do not create a subtype merely to share two fields; a small value object or helper can be clearer.
State identity, allowed values, optional fields and multiplicity. Decide which class validates each invariant so malformed states do not spread through unrelated UI code.

blocks.title: Build a thin application around testable services
paragraphs: Divide the path into input acquisition → parsing → domain model → processing → presentation. The command-line layer obtains a filename and commands, calls services and formats messages. It should not contain every filtering rule or equality implementation.

Define narrow method contracts first: parse(Reader) returns valid records or a documented failure; missingInspections(sections, inspections) returns a result without reading System.in; format(report) produces required text. This allows StringReader, small model objects and StringWriter to exercise the core independently.

Work through one valid example and one failure path before deciding that the architecture is adequate. Requirements can permit several correct class structures; a rubric checks responsibilities and behavior, not exact class names or paragraph wording.

blocks.title: Judge architecture by the program it enables
paragraphs: A good design assigns invariants, separates I/O from processing and gives tests a way to check observable requirements. Explain why a relationship exists instead of adding inheritance for its own sake.

cards.prompt: When does composition fit better than inheritance?
cards.answer: When an object contains or uses another object rather than satisfying its full substitution contract. Shared fields alone do not justify an is-a relationship.

cards.prompt: Why assign each invariant to a clear class or boundary?
cards.answer: Validation becomes consistent and testable; invalid states are rejected where they enter instead of forcing every unrelated caller to guess which checks already happened.

cards.prompt: What becomes easier when processing does not read from System.in?
cards.answer: Small deterministic tests can supply domain values directly, processing can be reused by another input layer, and UI errors do not become mixed with business rules.

cards.prompt: Can two different class diagrams both satisfy the same assignment?
cards.answer: Yes. Evaluate responsibilities, contracts, relationships, testability and required behavior. Matching one reference diagram is not a correctness criterion.

guided.title: Design a roof-inspection report
guided.prompt: An application reads sections and inspection entries, reports sections with no completed inspection, and writes a readable summary. Input locations are provided by the user. Invalid section identifiers reject the import. Propose a design and a small integration test.
rubric: Domain data is typed rather than stored as one raw String.
Parsing, processing and UI responsibilities can be tested separately.
Missing identifiers and resource failures have explicit handling.
An integration test connects valid parsing to the final report without awarding broad skill correctness.
reference: One design has Section and Inspection value types, a parser for each input, a ReportService and a thin CLI. Composition connects collections; no hierarchy is required by the stated behavior.

Use two sections and one completed inspection: only the other section is reported. Also check invalid IDs, an empty input, and write failures. A different design is valid if it meets the same contracts.
